reasons: Classification is correct: Section 11.1 imposes a five-year committed term and Section 11.2 provides exits only for uncured material breach or insolvency, so Corio (the Customer/licensee) has no convenience exit during a multi-year term — expressly walk-away territory under T4C and failing the 60–90 day/capped-fee fallback.

The redline is directionally right and actionable for our side: it grants Corio a 30 days' notice convenience right, in whole or in part, without penalty or early-termination fee, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid license, maintenance and MarketSite.net fees, tracking the model language.
No cut-back of a Vendor convenience right is needed because Commerce One likewise has none mid-term; the finding correctly notes this rather than over-editing.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing artifact — the inserted paragraph plainly states 'Corio may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice' — so it does not undermine the substance.
Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 60-day fallback.

Minor, non-disqualifying drafting nits: the new provision is appended to the p0098 'Effect of Termination' paragraph and the rendered text omits the '11.4' section number referenced in the rationale; renumbering/relocating the insert would tidy this up.
